thread:
Kai: Heads-up — noticed a weird p95 spike in the rollout dashboard for /v1/generate after we shifted canary weight to fallback. Endpoint breakdown shows p95 up ~120ms but raw logs from the canary hosts don't match. Anyone seen this?
Marta: Hmm, saw the spike too. Is this the dashboard that blends route-level percentiles with merged samples?
Ravi: If it's blending, p50/p95 can jump when fallback weight changes because the sample set changes. But 120ms sounds large. Do we have before/after sample counts?
Kai: Sample counts on the dashboard stayed ~constant. That's what makes it confusing — counts stable but percentiles moved.
Sasha: @Kai can you paste the route tags shown in the slice? Sometimes the telemetry tag for "route_origin" gets overwritten by the fallback path.
Kai: Sure — slice metadata shows route_origin=client, fallback_weight=0.2, route_variant=canary.
ops-bot: deploy: rollout weight changed — service/generate set canary weight 0.8 -> 0.6 at 2025-11-10T14:05:11Z :information_source: 
Emily: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the dashboard is merging tdigest rollups from multiple ingest windows with different compression leading to p95 drift, or 2) some requests were re-routed through a proxy adding ~100ms.
Ravi: Good points. I can run a quick query against raw traces. Suggest using this ad-hoc query to compare sample origins: 
```
SELECT origin, count(*) as cnt, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) as p95
FROM traces
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND time > now() - 30m
GROUP BY origin;
```
Marta: Also check KV-cache hit tag. If cache-hit labeling changed when fallback started, that will change the latency distribution without affecting total count.
Kai: Ran Ravi's query — pasted results in logs channel. origin=proxy cnt=320 p95=340ms; origin=canary cnt=1280 p95=98ms; origin=fallback cnt=80 p95=410ms. But dashboard showed merged p95 ~220ms which doesn't match weighted merge either.
Sasha: That suggests the dashboard merge weight calculation may be using per-rollup percentiles then averaging rather than recomputing percentile from merged samples. When you average p95s you get nonsense.
Emily: Yep. We had that bug in the legacy rollup code — merge-mode "per-aggregate-percentile" vs "reconstruct-sample" options. Which mode is the console using for route-merge?
Ravi: Console currently uses tdigest rollup merge (approx_merge) for memory reasons; that should be fine if all nodes use same compression params. If nodes differ, merged p95 can be off.
Kai: Can we add an annotation to the rollout panel indicating "merged percentile may be approximate when routes include fallback/proxy"? Users keep assuming exact.
Marta: Better — add a toggle to show raw-origin p50/p95 lines alongside merged line. Low effort and helps debugging.
ops-bot: ticket created: #ENGPLAT-1189 — "Show origin-split percentiles and add merge-mode note on rollout panels" assigned to platform-telemetry.
Ravi: Action items: I'll validate tdigest compression params across ingesters. Sasha can you add the origin-split lines to the panel (UX minimal). Kai, can you capture a small repro (console snapshot + raw query) and attach to the ticket?
Kai: Yep, I'll attach snapshots and the raw query results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Emily: Also recommend we log the merge-mode and compression version in the panel metadata so future puzzlers see it immediately.
Sasha: Agreed — adding that to the ticket.
Ravi: I'll follow up in ~30m with findings from the compression check.
Kai: Appreciate it. Leaving channel for now, will ping when I post the repro.
